project: Recover CLI Start, Status, and Result Loopback Against Deterministic Factory Sessions
description: Recover the dynamic workflow CLI run/status/result path by routing sync start, async start, status polling, result retrieval, and supported inspection commands through deterministic Factory Session fixtures. The intent is to restore customer-testable CLI behavior without waiting for the real JavaScript runtime, HTTP API wiring, or dashboard UI.

context.customerAsk: A user can start a JavaScript Factory Session from the CLI in sync or async mode, poll status, and retrieve final or partial result data from deterministic provider fixtures.
context.problem: The earlier dynamic-workflows-cell-cli-run-status-result work item is blocked by paired plan token work-plan-55 failing immediately after manual repair. The CLI loopback still needs recoverable run/status/result behavior, but it should not wait on the real JavaScript runtime, API handlers, dashboard UI, or the failed plan token.
context.solution: Create a narrower CLI-only recovery batch that uses completed mock provider fixtures and shared Factory Session execution request/status/result/dispatch/artifact types. Normalize CLI input through shared domain or apisurface helpers, render concise human output and deterministic JSON output, and verify sync, async, timeout, cancellation, inspection, and error paths with focused Go tests.

acceptanceCriteria: A sync CLI run of the deterministic fixture reports a completed outcome and includes either the expected structured result or the expected stable result hash.
An async CLI run returns a durable Factory Session id, and follow-up status/result commands report the same fixture state using that id.
A timed-out sync run reports timeout without claiming completion, and cancel-on-timeout behavior is visible when requested.
CLI output is concise for humans and deterministic for JSON across started, running, completed, timed-out, failed, not-ready, missing-session, and conflict outcomes.
Focused CLI tests cover not-ready result, missing session, unsupported mode, bad source, and requestId conflict paths.
Typecheck, lint, and focused tests pass, including go test ./pkg/cli/session ./pkg/cli/workflow ./pkg/factorysessionexecution.

userStories.title: Run a Fixture Synchronously to Completion
userStories.description: As a CLI user, I want a sync run command to execute a deterministic JavaScript Factory Session fixture and return the completed result so that I can verify the run loopback from the terminal.
acceptanceCriteria: A sync run against the fixture exits successfully when the fixture reaches completed state.
Human output clearly reports the completed outcome without dumping verbose internal state.
JSON output includes deterministic session identity/status fields and either the expected structured result or the expected stable result hash.
CLI input handling for source, args, requestId, wait, and timeout uses shared execution/domain normalization rather than transport-specific duplicate rules.
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Start Asynchronously and Inspect Status and Result
userStories.description: As a CLI user, I want an async start command to return a durable Factory Session id so that I can poll status and retrieve the fixture result later.
acceptanceCriteria: Async start returns a durable session id in human output and JSON output.
A follow-up status command using that session id reports the fixture state consistently.
A follow-up result command using that session id returns completed result data when the fixture is complete.
A result command against a still-running fixture reports not-ready without fabricating a final result.
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Report Timeout and Optional Cancel-on-Timeout
userStories.description: As a CLI user, I want a sync run with a short timeout to report timeout accurately and optionally cancel the session so that automation can distinguish incomplete work from completed work.
acceptanceCriteria: A sync run that exceeds its wait/timeout reports a timed-out outcome and does not claim completion.
JSON output for timeout is deterministic and includes enough state for automation to know the session did not complete.
When cancel-on-timeout is requested, output visibly reports that cancellation was requested or applied according to fixture behavior.
Tests prove both timeout-without-cancel and timeout-with-cancel behavior.
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Inspect Dispatches, Artifacts, and Events From the CLI
userStories.description: As a CLI user, I want supported inspection commands to list dispatches, artifacts, and polled events for a fixture-backed Factory Session so that I can understand partial session state before or after completion.
acceptanceCriteria: Dispatch list output shows deterministic fixture dispatch records when the CLI command exists for this surface.
Artifact list output shows deterministic fixture artifact records when the CLI command exists for this surface.
Event polling output reports fixture lifecycle/result events in stable order when the CLI command exists for this surface.
Unsupported inspection modes fail with a clear unsupported-mode outcome rather than falling through to ambiguous errors.
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Cover Recovery and Error Paths
userStories.description: As a CLI user or maintainer, I want invalid or incomplete fixture interactions to return stable errors so that recovery behavior is predictable and testable.
acceptanceCriteria: A missing session id returns a clear missing-session outcome in human and JSON output.
A bad source returns a clear source error without starting a session.
A repeated conflicting requestId returns a conflict outcome without creating ambiguous duplicate results.
Not-ready result, missing session, unsupported mode, bad source, and requestId conflict paths have focused CLI coverage.
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
